deadline_judgment.judgment: Cooperative cancellation plus byte ceilings is sufficient for this host-local read-only check under the named LOCAL_REGULAR_FILE_IO condition; it is not a hard worker wall-time guarantee.
deadline_judgment.reason: The worker now receives the same absolute monotonic deadline as its caller, refuses the next asset once expired, and raises at nonempty chunk boundaries. Unlike the prior implementation, an ordinarily progressing worker no longer processes the rest of its closure after caller timeout. Expiry is mapped to OperationalEnvelopeExceededError before observation construction or persistence. Combined with no-follow regular-file admission, bounded raw reads and generation/digest checks, this is a reasonable cooperative boundary for ordinary local storage.
deadline_judgment.limit: A thread in open, read or filesystem metadata I/O cannot be forcibly stopped by wait_for or the cooperative clock. Byte ceilings bound total bytes, not syscall latency. A stalled syscall can continue to occupy the shared executor until it returns. The new code does not prove process isolation or hard termination. N4 additionally identifies an avoidable read launched before checking an expired deadline.
deadline_judgment.required_condition: LOCAL_REGULAR_FILE_IO below must be recorded as an operating constraint; do not advertise this as a hard worker wall-time bound or extend it to hostile, remote, FUSE or potentially indefinitely blocking storage without a stronger worker lifecycle boundary.

L.title: Chunk expiry is tested after starting the next read
L.status: CONFIRMED by actual unbuffered read-position probe
L.scenario: The while condition performs handle.read before time.monotonic is checked. Calling _measure with an already-expired deadline on a nonempty file consumes 1 MiB, then raises MeasurementExpiredError; the new expiry test passes without checking that I/O happened first. In production, expiry can occur during path opening or processing the previous chunk, so the worker can launch an avoidable extra read after expiry. An empty/EOF read also bypasses that clock check. The caller remains wait_for-bounded and integrity checks are not bypassed, so this is Low under LOCAL_REGULAR_FILE_IO.
L.fix: Check the monotonic deadline immediately before each read, including the first and the EOF probe, and retain a post-read check to catch time spent inside I/O. Add a Spy asserting zero reads for an already-expired deadline and a controlled clock test proving no next read starts after expiry. This does not solve an already-blocked syscall; keep the named operating condition.
